name: The Kile Oak

location.address: 5939 East Beechwood Avenue, South Irvington, Indianapolis, Indiana

verified_sources: https://www.irvingtonhistory.org/visit/exhibits/kile-oak/ (Irvington Historical Society, the site's own steward and owner)
access: Free, a dedicated nature-study preserve open to adults and supervised children's groups, maintained by the Irvington Historical Society and Irvington Historic Landmarks Foundation. The wooded lot carries an informational sign and two bronze plaques (1973 and 1976). General visiting is possible on the lot; museum-staffed hours are Saturday-Sunday 1-4pm per the Society's own page, and the tree itself is fenced for protection.
transport: Irvington neighbourhood, Near Eastside Indianapolis; residential street, on-street parking
verify_notes: Named for Rev. Oliver W. Kile, a retired Ohio evangelist and Civil War veteran who bought the lot in 1901; his daughter Mae Kile campaigned for decades (from 1926) to save the tree and refused to sell to anyone who would not preserve it, keeping a visitor guestbook from 1928 that drew international signatures. The Irvington Historical Society bought the property in 1973 after her death. Named a Bicentennial Tree of the Year on 29 October 1976, cited as 'a living witness of the American Revolutionary Period'. The Society's own page (fetched directly) gives 87ft height, 5ft diameter, 190in (483cm) circumference, 122ft crown spread, calling it 'the largest Bur Oak in any metropolitan city in the State and the 6th largest in the State'; Wikipedia (also fetched directly) gives the same height/girth figures and a slightly wider age band, '300 to 500 years old'. Both sources are consistent; age_min/max set to the wider Wikipedia band to be conservative, age_estimate chip uses the Society's own narrower estimate. Confirmed alive and open as of a September 2024 storm (Hurricane Helene remnants) that caused damage, after which the site reopened once damaged branches were safely removed, per Wikipedia. location_precision confirmed: an exact street address, on a small dedicated preserve lot, matching the original Wikidata coordinate (Q130425459) almost exactly.
